Contributing to scMaSigPro

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for helping to improve scMaSigPro. This guide explains how to report a problem and how to propose a change.

Reporting a problem

Bug reports, questions and suggestions go to the issue tracker of BioBam/scMaSigPro. For a bug, include a small example that reproduces it (the bundled splat.sim data set is often enough), the full error message and the output of sessionInfo().

Proposing a change

The package is developed in spriyansh/scMaSigPro, where the checks run; BioBam/scMaSigPro receives its main branch at each release.

  1. Fork spriyansh/scMaSigPro and create a branch from main.
  2. Make one change per pull request, with its tests, its documentation and a NEWS bullet.
  3. Open the pull request against main of spriyansh/scMaSigPro and say what changes and why, and whether any result changes.
  4. The maintainer reviews it and merges it as one squashed commit.

For a larger change, open an issue first, so that the approach is agreed before the code is written.

Checks

Every pull request to main runs these GitHub Actions workflows:

  • R-CMD-check.yaml: R CMD check --as-cran, with the tests and the vignettes, on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu with the released R and on Ubuntu with R-devel. It must pass.
  • test-coverage.yaml: the tests under covr, with the coverage in the log. It must pass. For branches of spriyansh/scMaSigPro it uploads the coverage to Codecov, which reports the coverage of the package (target 80 %) and of the lines that the pull request changes (target 85 %); pull requests from forks get no upload.
  • pkgdown.yaml: builds the website. It must pass.
  • r-universe.yml: builds the package as R-universe does and runs BiocCheck.
  • lint.yaml: lintr with the settings of .lintr. It is advisory: it lists lints without failing.

Before you open the pull request, run in the package directory:

devtools::document()             # man/ and NAMESPACE; commit what changes
styler::style_pkg(indent_by = 4)
lintr::lint_package()
devtools::test()
spelling::spell_check_package()
devtools::check()

Style

  • R code follows the Bioconductor style: styler with 4-space indentation and lines of at most 80 characters, as .lintr sets. Pipeline steps are named sc.<verb>(), accessors and plots in camelCase and other functions in snake_case.
  • Documentation is written with roxygen2 in Markdown. man/ and NAMESPACE are generated by devtools::document(); never edit them by hand.
  • Documentation, messages and NEWS are in British English. A correct word that spelling::spell_check_package() does not know goes into inst/WORDLIST.
  • NEWS.md gets one short bullet per change, under the heading of the next version, saying what the code does now.
  • The Bioconductor package guidelines apply, since the package is prepared for Bioconductor.

Tests

The tests use testthat (edition 3). devtools::test() runs them all and devtools::test(filter = "show") runs one file. Outside devtools, set NOT_CRAN=true so that the snapshot tests run.

test-reproduce-masigpro.R and test-equivalence-masigpro.R compare scMaSigPro with maSigPro: with family = gaussian(), link = "identity" and offset = FALSE the results must be identical. They are skipped when maSigPro is not installed, so install it before you change the fitting code:

BiocManager::install("maSigPro")
devtools::test(filter = "masigpro")

tests/testthat/fixtures/golden-v0.0.4.rds holds the results of a fixed set of analyses. A change that alters results on purpose regenerates it with tests/testthat/fixtures/make-golden.R and says in the pull request which results moved; never edit the file by hand.

Code from other packages

scMaSigPro implements the maSigPro method from its publication (Conesa et al. 2006, Bioinformatics 22:1096), not from maSigPro’s source code. Do not copy or adapt code from maSigPro: write it from the published method and compare with maSigPro by its results only, as the tests above do. The same applies to code from any other package; cite the method you implement.
